title: Replit's CEO says it dropped Anthropic for OpenAI — Anthropic sources say the deal is still in place
subtitle: Amjad Masad told TechCrunch Disrupt that ChatGPT is now Replit Agent's default, citing cost and performance, but Replit's own September blog and a source close to Anthropic contradict the 'no longer working with' framing.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Replit CEO Amjad Masad told TechCrunch Disrupt on October 17 that his company is no longer working with Anthropic and that OpenAI's ChatGPT is now the default model inside Replit Agent, Replit's AI coding product. Masad cited cost and performance, said 'I think ChatGPT is better now' for Replit's use case, and framed the choice as temporary — calling OpenAI 'a better partner for now' rather than permanently. Users can still switch Replit Agent back to Claude from the model selector, and Replit's documentation continues to list Anthropic as a managed integration alongside OpenAI, Google, and OpenRouter.

The claim is contested. A source familiar with the deal told TechCrunch the partnership is still in place, and Replit's own September blog post names Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 as models running in Replit Agent's production environment. Replit announced OpenAI as a partner in August 2026 without saying it had dropped Anthropic. The CEO's framing — 'no longer working with' — is on the record, but the contractual status looks closer to a default change than a dissolution.

The underlying signal is still meaningful. Replit is one of the highest-volume consumers of frontier models in the coding-agent category, and defaults drive the vast majority of its API spend. If ChatGPT is now the default, the economics of that switch — cheaper tokens, better coding benchmarks, or both — will show up in Anthropic's revenue mix even if the integration stays technically live. The same shift has echoed on Cursor and other agent platforms over the last quarter, and it tracks with WSJ-reported OpenRouter data showing OpenAI's usage share rising from under 25% at the start of 2026 to nearly 50% last month.

A note for learners: in platform businesses, the model marked 'default' is almost always the model doing >90% of the work, even when alternatives are available. If you want to know who's actually winning a given category — coding, agents, image generation — ignore the model selector list and ask which option the product ships you to on the first click. That's the signal; everything else is marketing surface area.
